newsitem.title: BENIN: Benin parliament approves deficit 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Benin parliament approves deficit 1997 budget.

text.p: Benin's national assembly has approved the government budget for 1997, with spending up 20 percent from 1996 and a deficit which is higher in cash terms but slightly lower as a proportion of spending.

The budget, approved on SaturdayMby 58 votes to 20 with four abstentions, incorporates extra spending on public investment, a three percent basic pay increase for state employees and the recruitment of extra staff for health and education.
It also includes a 1.5 billion CFA fund to help relaunch the private sector.
The budget projects government revenue of 182.11 billion CFA francs against spending of 293.6 billion CFA.
The government plans to fund the 111.5 billion CFA deficit from gifts and loans, including those agreed with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in return for economic reforms.

The 1996 deficit was 94 billion CFA on spending of 243.2 billion CFA and revenue of 149.2 billion CFA. The 1996 deficit was just over 38 percent of budget spending; the 1997 deficit is just under 38 percent.
Parliament refused to accept the 1996 budget, forcing then-president Nicephore Soglo to promulgate it by decree.
Former Marxist military leader Mathieu Kerekou defeated Soglo in March multi-party elections, in a rare example of an African leader returning to power through the ballot box.
The budget draft project 1997 Gross Domestic Product growth at six percent and inflation at three percent against 5.8 percent and 5.5 percent in 1996.
